The parts of a scale and which of them may change

Source: R/tree.R
scale_tree.Rd

Lists the parts of a scale as a tree: its properties, the columns of the leaftable, and whatever a subclass adds. Each part carries one of three marks, defined by the identity of the scale (scale_id()), which is computed from the leaf column, the frame names and the frame codes:

Usage

scale_tree(x)

# S3 method for class 'scale_tree'
print(x, ascii = !isTRUE(l10n_info()[["UTF-8"]]), ...)

Arguments

x

A NestedScale or a ScaleProduct; in print(), the table scale_tree() returned.

ascii

Draw the branches with +, - and |. The default does so outside a UTF-8 session.

...

Ignored.

Value

A data.frame of class scale_tree, one row per part: part, the parent property it belongs to ("" for a property), its kind, shape, mark, the verb that changes it and a note. Printing it draws the tree.

Details

  • fixed: the part enters the identity. Changing it gives another scale, which data bound to the first one no longer matches; the route is to build a new scale.

  • derived: the part is computed from another one and is never set.

  • mutable: the part can change and the scale stays the same scale. The function that changes it is named where there is one.

The marks describe the object; they are not enforced on assignment. str() on a scale prints the same tree.

See also

scale_id(), scale_payload_parts()

Examples

scale_tree(scale_example())
#> <NestedScale> example@c24a3e23
#> ├─ leaftable   data.frame [7 x 6]            one row per leaf
#> │  ├─ item     leaf column          fixed
#> │  ├─ sector   frame                fixed
#> │  ├─ class    frame                fixed
#> │  ├─ group    frame                fixed
#> │  ├─ size     weight               mutable
#> │  └─ count    weight               mutable
#> ├─ frames      chr [4]              fixed    sector, class, group, item
#> ├─ members     list [4]             derived  from leaftable: sector 2, class 3, group 3, item 7
#> ├─ leaf        chr [1]              fixed    item
#> ├─ meta        list [4]             mutable  name, desc, weights, default_weight
#> ├─ attributes  data.frame [0 x 10]  mutable  attach_attributes_scale()
#> ├─ aliases     data.frame [0 x 4]   mutable  attach_aliases_scale()
#> └─ labels      data.frame [0 x 4]   mutable  attach_labels_scale()
tr <- scale_tree(scale_example())
tr$part[tr$mark == "fixed"]
#> [1] "item"   "sector" "class"  "group"  "frames" "leaf"  
scale_tree(scale_product(a = scale_example(), b = scale_example2()))
#> <ScaleProduct>
#> ├─ axes           list [2]                   one scale per axis
#> │  ├─ a           axis NestedScale  fixed    example@c24a3e23
#> │  └─ b           axis NestedScale  fixed    example2@f6854959
#> ├─ keys           chr [2]           fixed    a = item, b = period
#> ├─ joint_weights  NULL              mutable  reserved
#> └─ meta           list [2]          mutable  name, desc
